title: A claim becomes a test
caption: Six components must be fixed before a number counts: task and dataset (what is correct), model and metrics (what is better), the harness, the machine specification, the run rules and the report.

title: Which claim survives normalization?
caption: Five vendor spec cards — 8 TOPS at INT8, 15 TOPS at INT4, a proprietary latency, a two-generation-old MLPerf score, a peak at maximum batch — cannot be ranked until all five run the same task, model, machine state and boundary. Only then do the camera-trap gates (p99 ≤ 33 ms, battery, slice recall) decide.

title: One prompt, two measurements
caption: The same prompt costs 0.10 Wh measured at the accelerators and 0.24 Wh measured across the whole service — 58% accelerators, 25% host CPUs and DRAM, 17% idle reserve and overhead. The meter's dashed loop is the boundary.

title: 8.3 ms of work per 1,000 ms
caption: Keyword spotting runs one ~8.3 ms, ~3.3 mJ inference inside each one-second audio window — a 0.8% duty cycle. At that duty the standby floor sets battery drain: the efficiency that matters is the one that is off.

title: Same scores, different disagreements
caption: Both illustrative runs have 50 baseline errors and 60 compressed-model errors on 1,000 images. Count which model alone was right. With the chapter’s uncorrected McNemar statistic, 10 against 0 gives 10.0, above the 3.84 cutoff. With 30 against 20 it gives 2.0, below the cutoff.
